newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan plans to restore parliament supremcy.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan plans to restore parliament supremcy.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Monday he would seek to amend the constitution to restore the supremacy of parliament.

He said in a televised broadcast his Pakistan Muslim League Party (PML) and its allies had decided to repeal controversial parts of the Eighth (constitutional) Amendment, which empowers the president to sack a prime minister and dissolve parliament.

Sharif did not specify the exact portions of the amendment that was decreed by late military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq to acquire some powers previously exercised by a prime minister, including the power to appoint chiefs of armed forces.

He said his plan had the approval of President Farooq Leghari, who used his powers under the Eighth Amendment to sack then prime minister Benazir Bhutto on disputed charges of corruption and misrule and dissolve the National Assembly (lower house of parliament) on November 5.

Sharif, whose PML won a landslide victory in the February 3 elections, said he met Leghari at the president's home in Punjab province and "he willingly agreed to this decision" (to amend the constitution).
